newsitem.title: UK: British vices a very regional, varied affair.
newsitem.headline: British vices a very regional, varied affair.

text.p: Yorkshiremen are Britain's biggest drinkers, the Northern Irish smoke most heavily and northern England boasts the country's most reckless gamblers.
These details about British vices are unveiled by Britain's Office for National Statistics (ONS) in its annual survey on family spending, released on Thursday.
Image-conscious South Easterners, Londoners in particular, spend more on cosmetics and hair products than others.
Although Britain is supposed to be a nation of animal lovers, the South West boasts the population that splashes out most money on them.

The ONS survey found households in Yorkshire and Humberside spent an average of 12.20 pounds ($19.08) on alcoholic drink each week in 1995/96 while the population of Northern Ireland spent the least -- 7.80 pounds.
The Northern Irish are also Britain's most reluctant gamblers, betting only 2.20 pounds per week on average compared with the 5.30 gambled by happy-go-lucky northern households.

Northern Irish households made up for their puritanism in those areas by smoking more, on average, than any others in the country. An average household puffed its way through 8.10 pounds-worth of tobacco each week last year.
Householders in the East Midlands did not figure highly in the usual list of vices but that may have been because they tended to spend all their time with their cars.
Households in that region got through nearly 46 pounds a week in motoring costs last year, more than 50 percent more than the typical Yorkshire and Humberside household spent.
Having got their hair just right at a weekly cost of 2.20 pounds per household, people living in London and the South East then spent more on entertainment.
They forked out about 1.10 pounds each week on cinema and theatre tickets and nine pounds eating out.
Households in the North West and East Midlands shelled out 60 pence on films and plays and only 5.50 pounds on eating out.

The most sweet-toothed region of the country is East Anglia, the ONS survey found. East Anglian households bought sweets and chocolates worth 1.70 pounds each week on average in 1995-96, 60 pence more than the frugal Welsh.

The Scots guzzled most fizzy drinks on average but also appeared to be the best-informed people in Britain, spending an average of 2.60 pounds per week on newspapers, compared with just 1.90 by the average Yorkshire household, who were presumably too busy drinking.
